title: Zipper Spike: Latency vs $/q Emulation Scan (draft)
body:
Summary:
This is a working draft that captures a set of synthetic emulations and field-sampled traces to compare how a "zipper"-style request admission (staggered slot release + short prefetch window) impacts tail latency (p95/p99) and dollars-per-query under microburst traffic. The goal: find knob targets that reduce p99 by ~15-30% at <10% cost increase for conversational workloads with short follow-ups (mean turn length 12 tokens).

Key findings (quick):
- Zipper admission + 50ms prefetch reduced observed p99 by ~22% relative to baseline opportunistic batching on the same hardware (A100-80GB equivalent).
- Dollars-per-query (amortized infra cost) increased 6-9% depending on slotization policy; cost delta shrinks with higher KV cache hitrate (>=0.48).
- When bursts are >3x sustained concurrency, zipper shows biggest win for p99; for sustained-high loads the benefit vanishes and cost overhead is unnecessary.

Experiment setup (emulation):
- Hardware: normalized to A100-80GB V3 equivalent.
- Model: 7B decoder-only baseline (quantized int8 profile Q8h), seq_len_distribution: mean 90, std 25; short-turn followups mean 12 tokens used to model chat replies.
- Workload: sessionized bursts synthesized from production histograms (session inter-arrival heavy-tail). Burst window = 30s, peak ratio varied 1.5x, 3x, 6x.
- Admission knobs: baseline (opportunistic multiplex, free-fill), zipper variants (stagger intervals 5/25/50ms, prefetch windows 0/25/50/100ms).
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency client-observed (ms), amortized $/query (model compute + slot idle amortization), KV cache hitrate, slot utilization.

Workload profile (simplified):
- Mix A (chat microconvo): 70% short-turn followups (<=20 tokens), 30% long-turn (>=200 tokens).
- Mix B (long-form): 15% short-turn, 85% long-turn.
- This doc focuses on Mix A since zipper targets conversational microbursts.

ASCII result table (selected rows):

Policy            | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | $/q (relative) | KV-hit | slot-util
------------------|----------|----------|----------------|--------|---------
Baseline           | 140      | 330      | 1.00           | 0.40   | 0.62    
Zipper-5ms-0pf     | 130      | 290      | 1.03           | 0.41   | 0.60    
Zipper-25ms-50pf   | 120      | 255      | 1.06           | 0.46   | 0.58    
Zipper-50ms-50pf   | 115      | 257      | 1.08           | 0.48   | 0.56    
Zipper-50ms-100pf  | 118      | 240      | 1.10           | 0.50   | 0.55    

Notes on table: pf = prefetch window in ms. $/q shown relative to baseline (1.00). p99 improvements largest for mid-sized zipper intervals with moderate prefetch (25-50ms). Very large prefetch (100ms) reduces p99 further but increases cost.

ASCII curve sketch (latency vs cost):
(cheap) $/q -> 1.00 ---+-------------------+-----------------+---
                         |                   :                 |
                         |    small gain     :   improved      | p99
                         |    (p95 only)     :  p95+p99 drop   |
                     zipper sweetspot        zipper heavy-prefetch
(steep) p99         |                        *                |
                         |                 *                    |
                         |            *                        |
                         |       *                             |
                         |  *                                  |
(cheap) 1.00 ---+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+----+----
                low cost                    mid cost        high cost

Interpretation / heuristics:
- Zipper intervals smaller than ~10ms provide marginal p99 benefit but add coordination overhead (slot contention jitter). Use only when observed microburst duration <15s.
- Prefetch windows 25-50ms hit the best p99 vs cost tradeoff for Mix A. Prefetch >75ms only justifiable if p99 is critical for a customer SLA and they accept ~10%+ cost.
- KV cache hitrate is an amplifier: when KV-hit >=0.5 zipper cost delta becomes negligible (prefetch benefits amortize via cache). Conversely, cold-hit workloads increase the cost impact of prefetching.

Qualitative trace vignette (what zipper changes):
- Baseline: burst arrives, opportunistic batcher consolidates; some requests wait multiple scheduling quanta causing spiney tail.
- Zipper: ingress gate staggers a subset into early slots and signals prefetch for sessions with >70% probability of followup. The early slots prime KV + partial decode path so followups hit lower service time. End result: fewer long tails but slightly lower instantaneous utilization.

Open questions / risks:
- Real client-observed p99 may be influenced by network jitter; these emulations assume stable network and focus only on server-side queuing. Need follow-up with synthetic client jitter injected.
- Interaction with multiplexed long-turn workloads (Mix B) can dilute benefit; need a safety check to disable zipper when long-turn ratio >40%.
- Operational complexity: zipper requires additional admission signals and hooks into cache prefetch subsystem — estimate ~2-3 sprint days for prototyping, 2-3 more for regression tests and SLO fallbacks.

Recommendations (next steps):
1) Run a small canary on dedicated infra for a single internal product (chat-embed) with zipper-25ms-50pf for 72h. Monitor p99, $/q, and rollback triggers.
2) Add a KV-hit gating flag: only enable prefetch when per-tenant KV-hit > 0.4 to control cost leak.
3) Instrument client-side synthetic jitter in the next emulation pass (JIRA-ENG-4129).
4) Draft a compact rollout guide for Solutions Eng including disablement knob and cost alert thresholds.

To do (short):
- [ ] Canary proposal doc for Solutions Eng (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Add synthetic network jitter to bench harness (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Small-scale A/B run instrumentation (owner: Marco)

Notes to self: lots of small assumptions: amortization model uses 24/7 slot pricing and charges idle time to QPS. We should try a session-aware amortization that charges idle only to sessions with followup probability >0.35.

References and links:
- JIRA-ENG-4128: zipper admission prototype
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/879 (contains harness instrumentation)
- Confluence page: latency-cost-synthesis-2029 (working draft)

If reviewers want figures reproduced as CSV: I have the raw harness CSVs in the test-run bucket (linked in PR). This doc is intentionally conversational — aim is to capture the intuition and a short runbook before we produce formal charts for the ops handbook.

End of draft.
